title: Arthur Young's quest to invent the Bell helicopter
summary: Jeffrey Mishlove tells of Arthur Young's quest to invent the Bell helicopter, about 1926-1947 at Washington, D.C., and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.
place_text: US Patent Office, Washington; Bell Helicopter

tellings.quote: So he went to the patent office in in Washington and looked for unsolved problems.

plain: A psychologist and interviewer named Jeffrey Mishlove, on Jesse Michels's podcast, tells the story of Arthur Young, the inventor behind the Bell helicopter. According to Mishlove, Young went to the patent office in Washington, the office that records inventions, to look for problems no one had solved, and picked the helicopter, working on it from the 1920s to the 1940s. Mishlove tells it to show the unusual mind of a man who later became interested in consciousness and the unexplained.
